problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$*
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/62377f3e744c5767927f9591b8c6e3335a8036cad5fe9c62f52c041b2db2bac8.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,x\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,0\le x\le y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/05de07930f6cacfd0a3a21045a95628891965bb69d5df1bef4dbeeab9e480b97.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}[\operatorname{sin}⁡z]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{y}\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[x]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})]}_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(0-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
